answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable deposit before it may trade. Like a yarrow cutting that must take root before it can wander far, an identity earns trust only after its stake is committed. If the agent cheats or spawns duplicates, the deposit is slashed, so a Sybil attacker must pay for every fake identity on the voyage to scale, and loses that capital when caught, making mass fakery unprofitable.
